text: Watch these two helicopters hit each other just a few feet above a landing pad near Mount Everest.
It happened Tuesday morning in Pheriche Nepal almost fourteen thousand feet up on the trail to Everest base camp.
One helicopter was flying cargo up from Lukla. The other was bringing two trekkers back from base camp.
Both tried to land on the same pad at the same time from opposite sides.
Just a few feet off the ground the spinning blades of one helicopter hit the other one.
A forty-seven year old trekker from India was killed and three others were hurt including both pilots.
So why is a blade strike so deadly?
A rotor like this spins almost four hundred times a minute.
The tips move close to five hundred miles an hour so one touch rips the blades apart.
Pheriche is too far from the nearest control tower so pilots there have to sort out landings with each other by radio.
Nepal's aviation office says early reports point to a mix-up between the two pilots.
The full cause is still under investigation.
With no roads up here helicopters are the only fast way in or out so pads like this stay busy every day.
